newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday remained at a standstill, feedlot sources said.
Active sales last week reportedly provided packers with comfortable cattle inventories so they were not aggressively pushing for new supplies this morning, sources said.
A few bids reported early at $62.00 per cwt were steady with sales late last week, but passed by owners pricing cattle from $64.00 to $65.00, cattle feeders said.
The late sales last week also generated firm price outlooks among some cattle market watchers.

Prices late last week rebounded to $62.00, the price level seen at the start of the week. Prices had dipped to $61.00 to $61.50 by last Wednesday before a CME live cattle rally and active wholesale beef sales spurred renewed cattle trade at the $62.00 level, sources said.
However, projections for firm prices were somewhat blunted by contined large numbers of market-ready cattle despite somewhat smaller estimated showlists this week compared with last week, they said.
The Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma showlist was estimated near 97,000 head, 6,500 less than last week. Kansas' showlist was pegged near 88,000, down 3,000, sources there said.
